items.title: Receiver fights High Court order to hand over No.1 Oxford Street Hotel to Cheddar’s company
items.description: The legal battle over the No. 1 Oxford Street Hotel in Accra has taken a fresh turn, with the Receiver/Manager of the property, Nii Amanor Dodoo, and Cola Holdings Ltd filing an appeal against a High Court order directing that the hotel be handed back to Kensington Residential Partners 1 Ltd. The appeal was filed after the High Court, Accra, Commercial Division 2, sitting as a vacation court on Friday, August 21, 2026, set aside the Receiver’s possession of the property and ordered its re-delivery to Kensington Residential Partners 1 Ltd, owned by businessman Nana Kwame Bediako, commonly known as Cheddar or Freedom Jacob Caesar. The Receiver has also applied for a stay of execution of the order pending the determination of the appeal. The application and accompanying affidavit, filed in connection with the dispute, contend that the ruling contained serious errors of law and that the court that heard the matter did not have jurisdiction to do so. The case centres on the Receiver’s possession of the hotel under arrangements involving Cola Holdings Ltd and the subsequent challenge by Kensington Residential Partners 1 Ltd. Receiver challenges ruling In the affidavit in support of the stay application, Nii Amanor Dodoo, who describes himself as the Receiver/Manager appointed by Cola Holdings Ltd to realise its security rights over the property, said the High Court ruling required him to immediately surrender possession of the hotel. He further stated that the court made additional orders concerning steps he had taken after assuming possession of the property. The Receiver strongly disagreed with the decision and maintained that it was legally flawed. “I am advised by counsel and verily believe that the ruling of His Lordship Justice John-Mark Nuku Alifo is patently in error,” the affidavit stated. According to the Receiver, the decision was inconsistent with provisions of the Borrowers and Lenders Act, 2020 (Act 1052), particularly provisions relating to the enforcement of security interests when a borrower is in default. He argued that the ruling effectively required the restoration of conduct which, in his view, the law criminalises. “I am advised by counsel that the ruling flies in the face of the statutory provisions in the Borrowers and Lenders Act, 2020 (Act 1052) including provisions which make it a criminal offence for a borrower in default to stand in the way of possession being taken by the lender against a registered security interest. The ruling, in effect, is seeking to have criminal conduct restored,” he stated. Jurisdiction becomes key issue A major plank of the appeal is the contention that the vacation judge who heard the application did not have jurisdiction over the particular case. The Receiver’s affidavit states that the substantive matter was pending before Commercial Court 6, while the Judicial Service’s published arrangement for the vacation courts indicated that cases from Commercial Court 6 were to be assigned to the vacation judge sitting in Commercial Court 8. The affidavit said counsel for the Receiver initially went to Commercial Court 8 to ensure that the case was placed on the docket, but was informed that the docket was not available there. It was subsequently discovered that the matter had instead been sent to Commercial Court 2. The Receiver said the clerk at Commercial Court 2 could not explain why the docket had been brought to that court. The affidavit further states that another application connected to the dispute, involving a request for an injunction, had also apparently been placed before Commercial Court 2, although it was expected to go before Commercial Court 8. That application was not heard by the vacation judge and was instead deferred for determination by the substantive judge on October 22, 2026. The Receiver therefore questioned why the application resulting in the August 21 ruling had proceeded before Commercial Court 2. “It is not at all clear why His Lordship proceeded with hearing and ruling on an application which, according to the clear indication on the Judicial Service website, ought not to have been before him,” the affidavit stated. “Not having a warrant in respect of this suit, His Lordship had no jurisdiction in connection with it.” Constitution and Borrowers and Lenders Act cited The Receiver has also challenged the ruling on constitutional and statutory grounds. He contends that the decision was inconsistent with Article 296 of the 1992 Constitution, which governs the exercise of discretionary powers by public authorities. The appeal further argues that the High Court fundamentally misinterpreted the nature of a warrant for police assistance issued under Section 64 of the Borrowers and Lenders Act. According to the Notice of Appeal, the Receiver and Cola Holdings contend that the judge wrongly interpreted the warrant for police assistance as a warrant to take possession of the property. They are also challenging the decision on the basis that it was inconsistent with an earlier Court of Appeal decision cited in their submissions. The Notice of Appeal states that the appellants are dissatisfied with “the whole decision” and allege, among other things, “patent errors of law”. The appellants are seeking an order from the Court of Appeal setting aside the August 21 decision. Stay application The Receiver has urged the High Court to suspend the execution of its order while the appeal is pending, arguing that the appeal has a strong prospect of success. The affidavit describes the ruling as “unreasonable and irrational” and argues that immediate enforcement could have significant consequences for the parties involved in the dispute. “It is, therefore, in the interest of justice that execution of the orders of His Lordship be stayed pending an appeal which stands a great chance of success,” the affidavit states. The Receiver further indicated that, upon receiving the full ruling, his lawyers could take additional legal steps if the High Court did not set aside its decision. He said counsel would also, as a preliminary matter, ask the judge to correct what they consider to be an error in hearing and determining the application when the judge’s authority as a vacation judge allegedly did not extend to the case. The legal contest over the hotel therefore remains unresolved, with the next significant steps expected to centre on the application for stay of execution and the appeal before the Court of Appeal. The stay application has been scheduled for hearing on October 16, 2026. Motion for Stay of Execution Download

items.title: Thank You for Your Inattention to This Matter
items.description: This is an edition of The Atlantic Daily, a newsletter that guides you through the biggest stories of the day, helps you discover new ideas, and recommends the best in culture. Sign up for it here. One of Donald Trump’s current favorite riffs is to contrast how (in his opinion) the United States was seen under his predecessor, Joe Biden, and how it’s seen now. “They didn’t respect us two years ago. They laughed at us. NATO laughed at us. Everybody laughed at us,” Trump said at a summit in Turkey with allies last month . “They don’t laugh anymore. There’s no more laughing.” He’s right. It’s worse than laughing—they’re ignoring the president of the United States altogether. Trump styles himself as an heir to Theodore Roosevelt, but where Roosevelt said that America should speak softly and carry a big stick, Trump speaks loudly and carries a small one. Roosevelt’s bully pulpit has been reduced to a bullshit pulpit. This week, Trump made two announcements that, in the past, would have shaken the globe. Speaking to Fox News’s Trey Yingst about negotiations with Iran over the Strait of Hormuz, Trump said , “If Oman gets in the way, we’ll bomb the shit out of them.” In an ordinary world, such a threat would be a huge news event. Oman is not a hostile nation: It is one of the oldest U.S. allies in the Gulf region and has been a key intermediary in negotiations with Iran for years. Yet the news drew little governmental response. Neither Oman nor other U.S. allies in the region issued official comments or took any other action that suggested that they found the threat realistic. One possible reason for their muted response is that Trump has actually made this threat before: He said in May that if Oman didn’t cooperate with Americans’ plans for the strait, “we’ll have to blow them up.” Trump’s credibility has been undercut by his own capriciousness. Back then, he was threatening Oman over any negotiations that would imperil the neutrality of the Strait of Hormuz. On Tuesday, however, he posted a graphic on Truth Social that declared the strait a “NEW U.S. Territory.” (He’d previously said that he would soon declare it U.S. territory.) American annexation of an international waterway would represent a major shift in maritime legal precedent and require an enormous U.S.-military presence, but everyone knew that the pronouncement was nonsense. Trump has no means of controlling the strait, and The Washington Post reports that the Defense Department is actually considering a reduced regional footprint . Trump has also repeatedly promised that a deal with Iran is near completion, but after multiple false starts, these announcements fool only the markets . This is a big shift. During his first term, Trump garnered outsized attention for outrageous statements. In August 2017, for example, he created an international incident by threatening North Korea with “fire, fury, and frankly power, the likes of which this world has never seen before.” Trump clearly delighted in how the press and global leaders would scramble to respond to these provocations, and some people argued that he was pursuing Richard Nixon’s “madman theory” of keeping adversaries off balance. One can draw a direct connection between the fire-and-fury threat in 2017 and Trump’s friendly statements about North Korea’s Kim Jong Un in the past week. But over time, the world has grown jaundiced about Trump’s threats. The good news is that few world leaders and observers feel the need to take Trump’s outbursts seriously anymore. Fire drills driven by Trump’s idle talk fatigue the media, the public, and geopolitical systems, and they distract from more important stories. But that’s also the bad news. First, some of the things that Trump says are very dangerous. His favoritism toward North Korea could destabilize the region and encourage South Korea and Japan—to say nothing of Iran and other rogue states—to pursue nuclear-weapons programs. Second, he does occasionally follow through; Venezuela’s Nicolás Maduro may have thought that Trump was bluffing before he was arrested during an American incursion in January. Third, Trump needs credibility to enact his agenda, including to try to end the quagmire in Iran. On Wednesday, he said that he was “announcing the MOST CRUSHING ECONOMIC OPERATION EVER TAKEN AGAINST ANY COUNTRY!” All-caps notwithstanding, this declaration didn’t receive a great deal of attention. (“They have no clear plan, unfortunately,” one Middle Eastern diplomat told NOTUS .) In order for the sanctions regime he envisions to have its greatest effect, Trump will need the cooperation of allies as well as rival powers such as China. But years of empty boasts and months of feints on Iran mean that other world leaders don’t really heed Trump’s statements. He’s failed to enlist key allies in the war effort, and China has declined to take any concrete action in the strait, despite Trump traveling to Beijing in May to pressure Xi Jinping. This diminished respect given to presidential statements is self-evidently bad for Trump, and it does nothing to make America great again. But it’s also bad for the world. Even now, no other country has the power the U.S. has to maintain order, and the closest challengers, Russia and China, pursue systems that are repressive and dangerous. The U.S. can regain credibility only by using its rhetoric more carefully and matching its actions to its words—two things that are unlikely to happen under Trump. If he wants to be believed, the president needs to either surrender some American influence or show that his threats are real, and neither option is appealing. The costs of not being taken seriously are very serious indeed. Related: Oman has gone from “indispensable” ally to target of annihilation. David Frum: Only losers play the madman. Here are three new stories from The Atlantic : The White House freak-out over Natalie Harp From “indispensable” ally to target of annihilation Rachel Bedard: America’s gerontocracy needs a public physician. Today’s News Iran’s lead negotiator with the United States said that Iran must plan to counter U.S. sanctions as the Trump administration prepares new economic measures against Tehran. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is expected to announce details of the measures on Monday, after Trump vowed an “economic D-Day” against Iran. President Trump said that he will exempt 300,000 metric tons of imported ground beef from tariffs and that the beef will be sold at 25 percent below current market prices. A White House official said that Trump is expected to sign an executive order implementing the plan within the next two weeks. A charter plane crashed near a remote radar site in western Alaska yesterday afternoon, killing all eight people on board, including two pilots and six passengers; two of the passengers were members of the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. The cause of the crash is still being investigated. Evening Read Illustration by Matteo Giuseppe Pani / The Atlantic. Source: Getty. Why Is Everyone in Silicon Valley Talking Like That? By Lila Shroff Silicon Valley has long had its own dialect. Venture capitalists are always talking about the value of being “high agency” and making “orthogonal bets.” But lately, tech vernacular has taken a peculiar turn—people have started describing themselves as if they were chatbots. If you misspeak, maybe you’re “ hallucinating .” Don’t know the answer to a question? That’s because it’s not in your “training data.” Feeling forgetful? Perhaps you have a case of “ context rot ,” a phrase that refers to the degradation of a bot’s responses over a long conversation. “I’ve been telling my wife I have context rot for months,” Conor Bronsdon, the host of an AI-focused podcast, told me. Where I live, in San Francisco, such comparisons are inescapable. “I’ve described myself as high temperature,” a friend recently told me; in AI-speak, this means he is prone to randomness … Such speech easily comes off as unsettling, if not aggressively bleak: Why describe beautiful, tender life in detached, algorithmic terms? Read the full article. More From The Atlantic It’s low-calorie and packed with protein. Is it healthy? Joshua Sohn: Liberal families are looking pretty traditional. An unsettling glimpse into the GOP’s future President Trump has a pet-project docket at the national parks. Ossoff’s “Natalie” moment Culture Break Reflect. What’s happening to the WNBA isn’t normal, Jemele Hill argues. The league’s unprecedented success has come with unprecedented controversy . Read. Last year, Sophia Stewart recommended eight books for people who like to dabble in casual pursuits . Each read reminds us of the possibilities that lie in our hobbies—even the ones we’re bad at. Play our daily crossword. PS A decade ago, my colleague Spencer Kornhaber named FLOTUS , by the indie-folk group Lambchop, as one of the best albums of 2016 , likening the band to Bon Iver. Today, Lambchop is out with a gorgeous new record that actually features Bon Iver’s Justin Vernon. Lambchop’s music always has wry humor and good melodies, but I wasn’t prepared for the sumptuous harmonies on Punching the Clown . The band’s leader, Kurt Wagner, says that he was inspired by a chance hearing on the radio of lined-out singing, a centuries-old practice of church music that migrated from Britain to Appalachia. (For more on the style, read David Ramsey in the Oxford American .) If that seems like an odd basis for an indie record, the results speak—or sing—for themselves. — David Rafaela Jinich contributed to this newsletter. items.title: Partey begins new chapter in Saudi Arabia with Al Shabab
items.description: Ghana midfielder Thomas Partey has embarked on a new chapter in his club career after joining Saudi Pro League outfit Al Shabab as a free agent. The Saudi club confirmed the signing on Friday, unveiling the experienced midfielder on its social media platforms and describing him as a “legend”, while adding that the move “just feels right.” The transfer brings Partey’s European career to an end, following a season with Spanish side Villarreal. He had joined Villarreal after leaving Arsenal, where he established himself as one of the club’s key midfielders during a five-year spell. Partey, 33, made 167 appearances for Arsenal and scored nine goals during his time in north London. His career in Europe, however, stretches back further, with Atlético Madrid playing a significant role in his development. The Ghanaian came through the Spanish club’s youth system before progressing into the first team and making 188 appearances. He was part of the Atlético side that won the UEFA Europa League in 2018 and also earned a LaLiga winners’ medal from the club’s title-winning campaign. A decorated European career Partey’s move to Al Shabab adds another chapter to a career that has taken him from Ghana to the highest levels of European football. After developing at Atlético, he became a regular under Diego Simeone before securing a move to Arsenal at the beginning of the 2020-21 season. Although his Arsenal spell was interrupted by injuries at various stages, Partey remained an important figure in the club’s midfield and featured prominently during his five seasons with the Gunners. He subsequently moved to Villarreal before becoming a free agent and eventually agreeing to continue his career in Saudi Arabia. At international level, Partey has earned 60 caps for Ghana and scored 15 goals for the Black Stars. His international career was, however, overshadowed by controversy surrounding his participation at this summer’s World Cup after he was denied entry into Canada amid ongoing criminal proceedings in the United Kingdom. Partey denies allegations Partey has been charged with seven counts of rape and one count of sexual assault relating to allegations said to have occurred in London between 2020 and 2022. He has pleaded not guilty to all the charges. His trial, originally scheduled for November at Southwark Crown Court, has been postponed and is now expected to begin on June 8, 2027. Despite the controversy, Partey was able to feature in Ghana’s other three matches at the tournament, starting each of them. He played in the Black Stars’ 0-0 draw with England and their 1-0 defeat to Colombia, a result that ended Ghana’s campaign at the round of 32 stage. New challenge in Saudi Arabia Partey now turns his attention to Al Shabab and the next phase of his career in the rapidly expanding Saudi Pro League. He will not be short of familiar faces at his new club, with former Premier League players Josh Brownhill and Daniel Podence also on the team. He will also be reunited with former Atlético Madrid teammate Yannick Carrasco. For Partey, the move represents an opportunity to bring his experience at the highest level of European football to a new league, while Al Shabab will be hoping the Ghanaian’s physical presence, passing ability and experience can strengthen its midfield.

items.title: NSMQ 2026: St. Francis Xavier deny debutants Pentecost SHS one-eighth spot
items.description: One-time finalists, St. Francis Xavier Junior Seminary SHS, ended debutants Pentecost SHS, Koforidua’s hopes of reaching the One-Eighth Stage of the 2026 National Science and Maths Quiz (NSMQ) with a largely one-sided victory in the Preliminary Stage. Pentecost SHS were just four points behind after the opening round, but struggled to keep pace as the contest progressed. St. Francis Xavier led 18-14 after Round One, with Nana Bretu yet to score. The gap widened in the second round as St. Francis Xavier moved to 28 points while Pentecost SHS remained on 14 points. Nana Bretu were still without a point, leaving the contest increasingly tilted towards the two schools at the top. Pentecost responded in Round Three with seven points, but St. Francis Xavier maintained their lead with nine to take their total to 37 points. Nana Bretu finally got on the scoreboard with two points, but Pentecost still faced a 16-point deficit going into Round Four. St. Francis Xavier then opened up the contest. Their score climbed to 47 points, while Pentecost SHS reached 25 points and Nana Bretu nine. With a 22-point lead heading into the final round, the former finalists were firmly in command. The final round brought little change. St. Francis Xavier finished on 56 points, 31 points ahead of Pentecost SHS, who ended on 25 points. Nana Bretu managed 13 points. The result sends St. Francis Xavier into the One-Eighth stage and brings Pentecost’s first NSMQ appearance to an end. items.title: One killed in sword attack at Swedish school
items.description: One person has been killed in a sword attack at a high school in central Sweden, authorities have said. Police were called to the Brinell School in Fagersta shortly after 14:00 local time (13:00 BST) on Friday, where officers arrested an 18-year-old man. In an update on Friday, police said officers fired at the suspect before arresting and detaining him. He has not been named. Two teenage boys were seriously injured in the attack. Another person had minor injuries. Eight other schools in the area were placed under lockdown measures – which have now been lifted – while a state of high alert was declared in the Västmanland region following the attack. Sweden’s public broadcaster reported that the suspect was wearing a helmet. Local media also said he was a former student. Police said officers were now working to establish possible motives, adding that there was currently no danger to the public. In a post on X, Sweden’s Prime Minsiter Ulf Kristersson described the attack as a “serious incident,” and said “we do not know what lies behind the act, but we know that police are working very intensively”. Sweden’s King Carl XVI Gustaf said he received the news “with dismay and sadness”. In a statement, he said: “My thoughts are with those directly affected, as well as their families and loved ones.” Students at Brinell School had only just returned to the classroom following the summer break, with the new term beginning either on Monday or Wednesday this week, depending on the academic year. The school has just under 500 students on its roster, according to SVT, and is located 170km (105 miles) north-west of the capital, Stockholm. Sweden has experienced a number of attacks on educational institutions in recent years. The country experienced its worst-ever mass shooting in 2025 , where 11 people, including the gunman, died at an adult education centre in Örebro. This led to the government tightening the country’s gun laws after it was found that the suspect legally owned four rifles, three of which were found in the school where attack took place. Two teachers were killed in a violent attack on a secondary school in Malmo in 2022 – an 18-year-old student later confessed to the attack. In 2015, a teacher and a pupil were killed in a sword attack at a school in Trollh ä ttan .

items.title: Arsenal beat Lampard’s Coventry 3-0 in Premier League opener
items.description: Arsenal made the perfect start to their Premier League title defence with a stylish 3-0 win against Coventry in the opening game of the season on Friday. Mikel Arteta’s side brushed aside promoted Coventry in emphatic fashion at the Emirates Stadium, underlining their determination to retain the title. Kai Havertz struck early in the first half and Bukayo Saka doubled the lead before Martin Odegaard netted after the interval to complete Arsenal’s masterclass. The Gunners have not successfully defended the English title since the 1930s, but Arteta insisted this week his players are hungry for more silverware. Just 89 days after rounding off their title-winning campaign with a 2-1 victory at Crystal Palace in May, the champions showed no signs of being sated by that long-awaited triumph as they put Coventry to the sword. The only downside for Arsenal was the realisation they have to wait 10 days for their next game at Aston Villa. Worryingly for Arsenal’s rivals, they are only getting stronger and new signing Ezri Konsa was given a warm welcome when he was presented to fans before kick-off. The England defender completed his £51 million ($69 million) move from Villa earlier on Friday and could make his debut against his old club on August 31. Greek winger Christos Tzolis dazzled on his first league start for Arsenal after his close-season move from Club Brugge. Fellow new signing Bruno Guimaraes was hardly missed after being sidelined by an injury suffered in last weekend’s Community Shield win over Manchester City. Rampant Arsenal- Coventry were playing their first Premier League game since 2001 after winning the Championship last season to end their long exile from the top-flight. Having spent a season in the fourth tier, plunged into administration and twice been forced to ground-share away from Coventry in the 25 years since they were last in the Premier League, the return of Frank Lampard’s side was a feelgood moment. But Arsenal had no room for sentiment as they dispatched Coventry in merciless style. In their first home league game since being crowned champions last season, Arsenal strode onto the pitch with the acclaim of the sell-out 60,000 crowd ringing in their ears. The party atmosphere created by Arsenal’s jubilant fans in north London was a fitting backdrop to a swaggering performance. Tzolis, who provided two assists in the Community Shield, nearly bagged his first Arsenal goal in the opening minutes, firing just over from Odegaard’s pass. He went close again moments later with a close-range effort that was cleared off the line by Bobby Thomas. It was no surprise when Arsenal took the lead in ruthless fashion after 15 minutes. Coventry defender Milan van Ewijk surrendered possession carelessly on the right flank and Riccardo Calafiori pounced, whipping in a cross that Havertz met with a clinical low strike from just inside the penalty area. Arteta’s rampant team scented blood and went for the kill in the 23rd minute. Rice and Odegaard exchanged passes to work the ball out to Tzolis, whose cross was pushed out by Coventry keeper Carl Rushworth into the path of Saka for a simple close-range finish. Coventry had been reduced to helpless bystanders by Arsenal’s ceaseless pressing and clever movement. If it was not already over, Odegaard put the result beyond doubt in the 49th minute. Saka and Ben White teamed up to rip through the Coventry defence before Odegaard’s miscued shot from 10 yards scuffed past Rushworth’s weak attempted save. items.title: Affaire Algassimou : après avoir perdu sa fonction, le magistrat radié, perd sa dignité dans l’ordre national de mérite
items.description: Dans une série de décrets rendus publics ce vendredi 21 août, le président de la République, Mamadi Doumbouya, a pris deux nouvelles décisions concernant le magistrat Algassimou Diallo. Le premier décret porte retrait de son titre de Commandeur de l’Ordre national du Mérite de la République de Guinée. Cette distinction honorifique, qui récompense des services rendus à la nation, lui est ainsi retirée. Dans un second décret, le chef de l’État a radié Algassimou Diallo du corps de la magistrature. L’ancien avocat général près la Cour suprême perd ainsi son statut de magistrat et par conséquent de son statut d’agent de la fonction publique guinéenne. Ces deux décisions interviennent après sa révocation de la magistrature et viennent compléter les mesures prises à son encontre.

items.title: One dead as plane hits car
items.description: One person has been killed in western Canada after a small passenger plane struck a vehicle while making an emergency landing on a road, police said. The incident occurred on Thursday afternoon in Prince George, British Columbia, more than 700 kilometres (435 miles) north of Vancouver. Images of the incident show the small aircraft on the side of a road, nestled on the grass next to a forested area. “Police are saddened to confirm that there has been one fatality in this incident, an occupant of one of the vehicles,” the Royal Canadian Mounted Police said in a statement. It was not immediately clear if anyone on the plane was injured. Vanguard News The post One dead as plane hits car appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: À Taounate, le PAM veut réduire les fractures territoriales et renouer avec la jeunesse
items.description: À Taounate, le Parti authenticité et modernité (PAM) entend faire de la réduction des inégalités territoriales l’un des axes de son discours politique. Réunis vendredi au village de Ba Mohamed, dans la province de Taounate, les responsables du parti ont défendu une approche fondée sur la proximité, le développement du monde rural et la réconciliation avec une jeunesse confrontée à des difficultés persistantes en matière d’emploi, de formation et d’encadrement. Fatima Zahra El Mansouri, coordinatrice nationale de la direction collégiale du PAM, a résumé le constat en une formule : le « Maroc à deux vitesses » constitue, selon elle, « une réalité tangible » aujourd’hui. La responsable politique a rappelé qu’à son arrivée à la tête du secteur ministériel, elle avait souhaité redéfinir la notion de « politique de la ville », afin de ne plus la cantonner aux grandes agglomérations et de l’étendre à l’ensemble des provinces ainsi qu’au monde rural. Le développement rural au cœur du discours Pour illustrer cette orientation, El Mansouri a cité la province de Taounate, où neuf conventions de développement ont été signées. Elle a également évoqué des accords similaires conclus dans la province de Taza et avec des communes rurales, ainsi que 49 conventions dans la région de Fès-Meknès, accompagnées d’importantes enveloppes financières destinées à la mise à niveau des centres ruraux émergents. Ces investissements ne suffisent toutefois pas, selon la responsable du PAM, à masquer les difficultés auxquelles demeure confrontée la province de Taounate. Elle a salué les avancées réalisées par le Maroc au cours des 27 dernières années sous la conduite du roi, notamment dans le cadre du projet de « l’État social », tout en reconnaissant que le pays reste confronté à des contraintes importantes. Pour le PAM, la première d’entre elles est celle de la « justice territoriale et sociale ». El Mansouri a illustré cette fracture par le contraste entre deux jeunesses : celle d’un jeune né dans une grande ville, qui peut nourrir de grandes ambitions, et celle d’un autre né dans une province comme Taounate, susceptible de grandir « sans espoir ni rêve ». La responsable politique a appelé à ne pas éluder cette réalité. « Nous n’allons pas cacher le soleil avec un tamis », a-t-elle déclaré, avant de revenir sur les épisodes migratoires ayant concerné Sebta et Melilla. Elle les a interprétés comme le symptôme d’une crise de confiance entre une partie de la jeunesse, les institutions et la société. Une « réconciliation » avec les jeunes Dans ce contexte, le PAM entend défendre un nouveau « contrat social » accordant une place centrale aux jeunes. El Mansouri estime que cette catégorie dispose d’« énergies considérables » susceptibles de bénéficier au pays, à condition que les obstacles auxquels elle est confrontée soient effectivement pris en charge. Elle considère ainsi que le principal défi des prochaines années sera d’opérer une véritable « réconciliation entre les jeunes et la société ». Une entreprise qui, selon elle, ne pourra être menée qu’en s’attaquant collectivement aux questions de l’emploi, de la formation et de l’encadrement. La dirigeante du PAM a également défendu la méthode politique de son parti. Celui-ci, a-t-elle assuré, ne serait pas « un parti de rapports ou de solutions imposées depuis les bureaux d’études ». Il privilégierait au contraire des réponses élaborées à partir du terrain, « de bas en haut », après un diagnostic direct mené avec les populations. Les rencontres de proximité organisées par le parti constituent, à ses yeux, une traduction concrète de cette démarche participative. « Faire de la politique autrement » El Mansouri a par ailleurs retracé le parcours du PAM depuis sa création, affirmant que le parti avait construit son expérience « étape par étape », autour d’une ambition constante : « faire de la politique autrement ». Cette conception repose, selon elle, sur la proximité avec les citoyens et leur écoute. Elle aurait permis au parti de gagner la confiance des populations au niveau des collectivités territoriales et des régions et de parvenir à un bilan dont la responsable politique estime qu’il « fait la fierté de tous ses militants ». Elle a également attribué à cette implantation sur le terrain l’accession du PAM au rang de deuxième force politique du pays. Une position qui lui permet, selon elle, de jouer un rôle « actif et réussi » au sein du gouvernement, notamment à travers la conduite de chantiers dont les effets se font directement sentir dans la vie quotidienne des citoyens. La dirigeante du parti a enfin présenté le projet de « Tamghrabit » et l’attachement à la nation comme les ressorts des déplacements réguliers de la direction du PAM vers les territoires du « Maroc profond ». L’objectif affiché est double : écouter les populations des différentes provinces et soutenir les militants et candidats du parti. À Taounate, cette mobilisation concerne notamment Mohamed Hajira et Abderrahim Fouiker, cités par Fatima Zahra El Mansouri parmi les représentants du PAM que la direction entend accompagner. The post À Taounate, le PAM veut réduire les fractures territoriales et renouer avec la jeunesse appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: UK Travel Advisory: Nasarawa Government welcomes exclusion
items.description: By Edwin Phillip, Lafia LAFIA: The Nasarawa State Government has welcomed its exclusion from the latest United Kingdom travel advisory, describing the development as a reflection of the state’s efforts to maintain peace and security. Nasarawa is reportedly the only state in the North-Central region not included in the advisory restricting travel to the region. The state government said the development demonstrated that its sustained efforts to prevent insecurity and maintain peace were yielding positive results, adding that it would intensify measures to sustain and improve the prevailing security situation. This was contained in a statement issued on Friday by the Chief Press Secretary to Governor Abdullahi Sule, Mr Ibrahim Addra. According to the statement, the advisory, which was “still current as at 21st August 2026” on the UK Government website, was issued through the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO). It said the advisory advised against all but essential travel to states in the North-Central region, with Nasarawa excluded. The government said it received the development with humility and gratitude to God, adding that it was encouraged by the collective efforts of stakeholders to promote peace and security in the state. While commending President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, other governors and security agencies for their efforts in tackling security challenges across the country, the government acknowledged that more needed to be done. It said it would continue to work to sustain and improve the prevailing peace and security in Nasarawa State. “In Nasarawa, this positive outcome is also a reflection of the deliberate measures taken by the administration of Governor Abdullahi A. Sule to strengthen security, support security agencies and foster closer collaboration with communities and other stakeholders,” the statement said. Governor Sule appealed to residents to remain vigilant and continue supporting security agencies by providing timely and credible information that could assist in preventing crime and maintaining peace. items.title: NSMQ 2026: Tamale SHS sweep aside Kalpohin, Wenchi Methodist to reach one-eighth stage
items.description: ‎The Lions of Tamale had their eyes on the prey — and once they pounced, there was little escape. Tamale SHS tore through sister school Kalpohin SHS and Wenchi Methodist SHS in the Preliminary stage, turning what began as a close contest into a commanding victory to book their place in the One-Eighth stage of the 2026 National Science and Maths Quiz (NSMQ). ‎ ‎The opening round offered little between Tamale SHS and Kalpohin SHS, with just two points separating the sister schools. Tamale SHS led 19-17, while Wenchi Methodist had nine points. But the Lions began pulling away in Round Two, adding 18 points to reach 37 points, while Kalpohin SHS moved to 19 points and Wenchi Methodist to 11 points. ‎ ‎Round Three saw Tamale SHS and Kalpohin SHS both add nine points, leaving the Lions on 46 points and Kalpohin on 28 points, with Wenchi Methodist on 17 points. Tamale then produced its biggest burst in Round Four, adding 16 points to reach 62 points and stretching the gap over Kalpohin to 21 points. Wenchi Methodist was on 24 points. ‎ ‎The Lions also produced a perfect run in the True or False segment, answering all eight questions correctly to claim the Jupay Clean Sheet Prize. ‎ ‎The final round simply confirmed their dominance as the Lions added six points to finish on 68 points, leaving Kalpohin on 41 points and Wenchi Methodist on 30 points. ‎ ‎The final scores sent the Tamale camp into jubilation, with contestants and supporters celebrating a victory that had grown from a narrow two-point lead into a 27-point winning margin. The race for Tamasco, however, is far from over as they head on to meet stronger contenders on the One-Eighth stage. The 2026 National Science and Maths Quiz is produced by Primetime Limited and sponsored by the Ghana Education Service with support from Goil Plc, Prudential Life Insurance, Pepsodent, Trustur AI and Jupay Money Transfer. ‎ ‎The Broadcast on JoyNews is sponsored by: VitaMilk and Chartered Institute of Management Accountants. items.title: Le président chinois Xi Jinping félicite le Roi Mohammed VI à l'occasion de la Fête de la Jeunesse
items.description: Le Roi Mohammed VI a reçu un message de félicitations du Président de la République Populaire de Chine, M. Xi Jinping, à l'occasion de la Fête de la Jeunesse. Dans ce message, le Président chinois exprime ses sincères félicitations et ses meilleurs vœux à Sa Majesté le Roi. Se félicitant de l'amitié historique profonde unissant le Maroc et la Chine, M. Xi Jinping affirme que les deux pays sont restés, depuis l'établissement de leurs relations diplomatiques il y a 68 ans, attachés aux principes de respect mutuel, de dialogue sur le même pied d’égalité et de bénéfice réciproque, notant que les relations sino-marocaines connaissent un développement sain et stable. Tout en rappelant l’annonce de l'établissement du partenariat stratégique entre la Chine et le Maroc lors de la visite d'État effectuée par le Souverain en Chine en 2016, le Président chinois souligne qu’après dix années de développement, la confiance mutuelle entre les deux pays sur le plan politique s’est davantage consolidée, la coopération pratique a donné lieu à des résultats fructueux et les échanges culturels et humains n’ont cessé de gagner en dynamisme, faisant ainsi des relations sino-marocaines un modèle à suivre en matière de solidarité et de coopération entre les pays du Sud global. Dans ce message, M. Xi Jinping dit également accorder un grand intérêt au développement des relations sino-marocaines, faisant part de sa volonté à œuvrer de concert avec Sa Majesté le Roi pour consolider davantage l'amitié et la confiance réciproque entre les deux pays, approfondir la communication et la coopération dans tous les domaines, à l’aune du 10e anniversaire de l'établissement du partenariat stratégique entre le Maroc et la Chine, célébré cette année, à même de favoriser un développement stable et durable des relations bilatérales. items.title: I want presidency to tackle Nigeria’s national problems — Adebayo
items.description: Says competence, patriotism, public service should matter over wealth By Henry Umoru ABUJA: Ahead of the 2027 presidential election, the presidential candidate of the Social Democratic Party (SDP), Prince Adewole Adebayo, has said his ambition to become President is driven by the need to tackle Nigeria’s major national challenges, particularly insecurity and poverty. Adebayo said he was not seeking political office for personal wealth, recognition or career advancement, arguing that some of the country’s biggest challenges could only be effectively addressed by the Federal Government through the use of national institutions and resources. The SDP presidential candidate said a state governor could not, on his own, reorganise the Armed Forces or coordinate security operations across different parts of the country. He said his political ambition was therefore driven by the desire to use the powers of the presidency to address problems affecting Nigerians across the country. Adebayo also rejected the notion that political candidates must be wealthy to successfully contest elections, stressing that competence, patriotism and commitment to public service should matter more than personal financial strength. The 2023 presidential candidate of the SDP said he had spent the past two decades focusing on intellectual work and creating opportunities rather than accumulating personal wealth. He, however, pledged that his political movement would not rely on criminal activities or the pursuit of money to gain political power. Adebayo cited Section 5 of the Constitution, which vests the executive powers of the Federation in the President and makes the President the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces. He said the constitutional responsibility makes the presidency the most important platform for addressing challenges that affect the entire country. The post I want presidency to tackle Nigeria’s national problems — Adebayo appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ioba/Ouessa : La délégation spéciale communale sensibilise les populations sur la sécurité routière
items.description: Burkina – Ioba – Sécurité – Routière Ioba/Ouessa : La délégation spéciale communale sensibilise les populations sur la sécurité routière Ouessa, 20 août 2026 (AIB) – La délégation spéciale communale de Ouessa a échangé, le jeudi 20 août 2026, avec les autorités administratives, coutumières et religieuses ainsi que les populations, sur plusieurs questions liées à la protection des personnes et des biens et au développement de la commune. La rencontre présidée par le Président de la délégation spéciale (PDS) de la commune de Ouessa, Ismaël Sanogo a essentiellement porté sur la sécurité routière, la clôture du Centre médical (CM) de Ouessa en construction, l’ouverture et la gestion d’un cimetière laïc ainsi que l’établissement de la Carte d’identité biométrique de l’Alliance des Etats du Sahel (CIB – AES). Sur la sécurité routière, le commandant de la brigade territoriale de gendarmerie de Ouessa a insisté sur la nécessité du respect du Code de la route et du port du casque, invitant les usagers à adopter des comportements responsables afin de réduire le nombre des accidents. Le PDS communale de Ouessa, Ismaël Sanogo, s’est réjoui de la participation des différentes composantes de la communauté aux échanges et à la sensibilisation. « C’est un rendez-vous pour le développement de notre chère commune et la protection des personnes et des biens », a-t-il déclaré. La rencontre s’est achevée par des échanges avec les participants sur des points divers. Agence d’Information du Burkina FC/SZ-DNK

items.title: Tupac murder accused told police in 2008 his nephew fired fatal shots
items.description: The man accused of orchestrating the murder of Tupac Shakur told police more than a decade later that he handed the gun used in the drive-by shooting to a passenger who then passed it to his nephew who opened fire on the rapper. Duane “Keffe D” Davis is on trial in Las Vegas, charged with one count of murder with a deadly weapon over the killing of the rap superstar in 1996. On Thursday jurors heard a recording of a police interview with Davis in 2008. Prosecutors allege that although Davis did not fire the gun that killed Shakur, he ordered the shooting and supplied the deadly weapon to further criminal conduct for the gang he helped lead. Davis, 63, has pleaded not guilty. His lawyer Michael Sanft has argued that what his client had previously said of his involvement cannot be believed. Shakur’s murder is a cold case that has gripped the public’s fascination for 30 years. Prosecutors allege Davis planned the 7 September 1996 shooting after his nephew Orlando Anderson was involved in a fight with Shakur in Las Vegas hours earlier. They argue that Davis believed the attack on his nephew could not “go unanswered”. Central to the case are testimonies by Davis in the formerly secret 2008 police interview and, later, in a 2019 memoir he co-authored called Compton Street Legend. Prosecutors on Thursday played the 2008 interview Davis conducted with Los Angeles Police detectives Daryn Dupree and Greg Kading, who were investigating the death of another rapper, Chris Wallace, aka The Notorious B.I.G. Davis described the moment the Cadillac he was a passenger in stopped alongside the car Shakur was in. “Yeah, if we would’ve been on my side, I would’ve blasted,” Davis said, according to a transcript. According to the transcript, Davis said in the interview he passed his gun back to Deandre “Big Dre” Smith, but Smith did not want the weapon. Anderson, who was also in the back seat, took the weapon and started firing, Davis said. Anderson died a decade before the interview, having denied any involvement in Shakur’s murder. A 1996 photo of rapper Tupac Shakur (L) and Marion “Suge” Knight displayed during the murder trial One of the detectives, Kading, told Davis in reference to a deal for his information: “Nothing you say today can be used against you.” But prosecutors say any agreement was negated when Davis went public with his version in his memoir several years later. The prosecutor said the book shows Davis was “mad” after his nephew was involved in a fight with Shakur in a Las Vegas casino, with Davis writing: “Them jumping on my nephew gave us the ultimate green light to do something to their ass.” In the memoir he claimed he was inside the vehicle when Tupac was shot, and “tossed” the gun used to kill him into the backseat. Davis has since distanced himself from the book, saying he did not write all of it and that parts were fictionalised to sell more copies. In the interview played to court, Davis said he repeatedly spoke with Sean “Diddy” Combs and discussed killing Shakur. The detectives questioned Davis about meetings with Combs during Bad Boy Records tour stops in San Diego, Anaheim, Irvine and Las Vegas. “Which of those four is it when you talk to him about murdering Tupac?” Kading asked, according to a transcript shown in court, as reported by Reuters. “It was really about both of them, yeah, either one of them,” Davis responded. “Tupac and Suge?” Kading asked, referring to Death Row Records founder Marion “Suge” Knight, who was with Shakur in the vehicle during the shooting. “Yeah,” Davis responded. Representatives for Combs did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Reuters. However, Davis’ lawyer Sanft asked jurors earlier in the trial: “What facts do you have to support any of what Keffe D said in any of his interviews or the book?” “You have to ask yourself the question: If I just say things, is that going to end up being one of those things where I’m going to be handed up for a murder by just repeating that fiction? I keep repeating that? The answer is no. You have to corroborate everything I say in order for it to be true. Otherwise, it’s just that.” Sanft has also said prosecution witnesses were unreliable and the police investigation was riddled with issues. A former Las Vegas homicide detective told the jury earlier this week that no witnesses had been able to identify the shooter. Later, a former member of Shakur’s entourage, James “Mob James” McDonald, gave evidence that even though he was not there to witness the shooting, those who were there that night within Shakur’s circle had quickly communicated who was responsible. “It was a gang war. People were getting hurt. People were being sought,” he said. “Orlando (Anderson), him and certain other people were being sought because people wanted to kill them.”

items.title: Ioba/Dissihn : une opération spéciale d’enrôlement de la CIB-AES lancée à l’occasion de l’Assomption
items.description: Burkina-Ioba-AES-Souveraineté Ioba/Dissihn : une opération spéciale d’enrôlement de la CIB-AES lancée à l’occasion de l’Assomption Dissihn, 20 août 2026 (AIB) – La commune de Dissihn a accueilli, du 13 au 16 août 2026, une opération spéciale d’enrôlement pour la Carte d’identité biométrique de l’Alliance des Etats du Sahel (CIB-AES), à l’occasion de la fête de l’Assomption, a constaté l’AIB. Placée sous le thème « Fêtons l’Assomption à Dissihn avec nos CIB-AES », l’opération vise à permettre aux populations de la commune de se faire enrôler pour l’obtention de la nouvelle pièce d’identité de l’Alliance des États du Sahel (AES). Dès les premières heures de la matinée du 13 août 2026, la cour de la Maison des jeunes de Dissihn a enregistré une forte affluence. Hommes, femmes, jeunes et les enfants ont convergé vers le site pour se faire enrôler. Présidant la cérémonie officielle de lancement, le président de la délégation spéciale (PDS) de Dissihn, Benjamin Nana, a indiqué que cette opération constitue un accompagnement des autorités centrales à la célébration de l’Assomption dans la commune. Selon lui, si la fête de l’Assomption est célébrée sur toute l’étendue du territoire burkinabè, celle de Dissihn revêt un caractère particulier. « C’est dans ce sens que les autorités au niveau central ont décidé de nous accompagner dans notre fête en offrant un cadeau », a-t-il déclaré. Ce « cadeau » consiste en la mise à disposition d’une équipe de l’Office national d’identification (ONI), venue de Ouagadougou et de Gaoua avec l’appui de l’équipe locale de Dissihn. Pendant quatre jours, les agents sont chargés d’enrôler les populations désireuses d’obtenir la CIB-AES. Devant les corps constitués et les leaders religieux, le PDS a invité les populations à saisir cette occasion pour se faire enrôler. Il a particulièrement exhorté les parents à faire établir la CIB-AES de leurs enfants, dès l’âge de cinq ans et jusqu’à l’âge adulte. À l’issue des interventions, le PDS suivi de ses collaborateurs, a été le premier à se soumettre à l’opération d’enrôlement, donnant ainsi le top de départ officiel. L’opération s’est poursuivie à la Maison des jeunes de Dissihn, jusqu’au 16 août 2026. Parmi les bénéficiaires, Mariette Hien, après son enrôlement, n’a pas caché son soulagement, estimant que l’obtention de cette nouvelle pièce d’identité constituait jusque-là une source de préoccupation pour elle. Agence d’information du Burkina JBD/SZ-DNK

items.title: 2027: Senator Imasuen disowns Edo South poster, threatens legal action
items.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA: Chairman, Senate Committee on Ethics, Code of Conduct and Public Petitions, Senator Neda Imasuen (APC, Edo South), has denied any involvement in a political poster portraying him as one of the contenders for the Edo South senatorial seat in the 2027 election. Imasuen said his name and photograph were used without his consent, describing the poster as misleading. He stressed that he was not the candidate of the Labour Party or any other political party for the 2027 election. In a statement he personally signed, the senator said he had accepted the outcome of the relevant political process and had not authorised any campaign material presenting him as a contender in the 2027 election. He warned Prince Omokhodion Okojie and others behind the poster to stop using his name, photograph and identity for political activities without his consent. Imasuen said any further unauthorised use of his identity could attract legal action, and urged members of the public to disregard political materials presenting him as a candidate without his approval. The controversy followed the circulation of a poster for the 2027 Edo South senatorial election bearing Imasuen’s photograph among those listed as possible contenders. Reiterating his position, Imasuen said he had no connection with the poster and had neither approved nor authorised its production or circulation. He maintained that he was not the candidate of the Labour Party or any other political party for the 2027 election and warned those behind the material against further use of his identity without permission. The post 2027: Senator Imasuen disowns Edo South poster, threatens legal action appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Burkina : Le processus de formulation du cadre de programmation pays de la FAO pour la période 2027-2031 officiellement lancé
items.description: Le Cadre de programmation pays (CPP) de l'Organisation des nations unies pour l'alimentation et l'agriculture (FAO) couvrant la période 2023-2026 arrive à terme en décembre 2026. Afin de disposer d'un nouveau CPP pour la période 2027-2031, la FAO et le gouvernement burkinabè ont enclenché le processus de formulation. Le lancement officiel du processus est intervenu ce vendredi 21 août 2026 au cours d'un atelier organisé à cet effet. L'atelier de ce jour devrait permettre de partager avec les participants la démarche méthodologique proposée, renforcer la compréhension commune des résultats attendus, recueillir les orientations des différentes parties prenantes et valider la feuille de route qui guidera les prochaines étapes. Il faut noter que le CPP est le principal instrument de coopération entre la FAO et le Burkina Faso. Il définit les domaines prioritaires dans lesquels la FAO met son expertise technique et ses ressources au service des priorités nationales de développement. Ernest Moïse Mushukuru, représentant de la FAO au Burkina Faso a réaffirmé l'engagement de son organisation à accompagner le Burkina Faso Le document en élaboration est le quatrième du genre. Il intervient dans un contexte marqué par les efforts des autorités nationales en faveur de la sécurité alimentaire, la résilience des ménages ruraux, le développement des chaînes de valeur agricole ainsi que le renforcement de la cohésion sociale. "Cette nouvelle programmation devra donc répondre à ces enjeux tout en valorisant les opportunités offertes par le potentiel agricole, pastoral, forestier et halieutique du pays », a indiqué le représentant de la FAO au Burkina Faso, Ernest Moïse Mushukuru. Ibrahim Patindé Alassane Ouédraogo, chargé de programmes de la FAO au Burkina a fait savoir que le processus sera participatif Il a fait savoir que son institution souhaite que le processus de formulation du CPP soit fondé sur trois principes fondamentaux que sont l'appropriation nationale par les institutions, l'inclusivité des différents acteurs ainsi que l'alignement avec le cadre stratégique 2022-2031 de la FAO et ses quatre améliorations. Ernest Moïse Mushukuru n'a pas manqué de réaffirmer l'engagement de la FAO à accompagner le gouvernement burkinabè dans sa vision d'une agriculture plus productive, plus résiliente, plus inclusive et plus durable. Alassane Guiré, directeur de cabinet du ministre de l'agriculture a présidé l'atelier de lancement au nom du ministre Pour la formulation du nouveau CPP, deux consultants nationaux ont été mobilisés. Ils seront appuyés dans leur démarche par le Bureau régional de la FAO basé au Ghana et l'équipe technique de la représentation de la FAO au Burkina. Ibrahim Patindé Alassane Ouédraogo, chargé de programmes de la FAO au Burkina a fait savoir que le processus sera participatif avec l'implication des départements ministériels tels que celui de l'Agriculture, de la Santé, de la Jeunesse, de la Famille, etc. Il a ajouté que des rencontres sectorielles et régionales seront aussi organisées afin de parvenir à un document final consensuel en adéquation avec les référentiels adoptés par le Burkina. Vue des participants ‎ L'atelier de lancement du processus de formulation du nouveau CPP, a été présidé par le ministre de l'agriculture, représenté par son directeur de cabinet, Alassane Guiré. Celui-ci a exprimé la gratitude du gouvernement à l'endroit de la FAO pour son appui constant au développement du pays. Pour le nouveau référentiel qui va régir la coopération entre l'organisation et le gouvernement burkinabè, il a souhaité que celui-ci s'inscrive pleinement dans l'architecture du système national de planification et s'aligne sur les référentiels en vigueur qui sont le Plan relance et l'Offensive agro-pastoral, hydraulique et halieutique 2026-2028. Alassane Guiré a ajouté que la pertinence des priorités à identifier, la durabilité des interventions, l'équité, l'ancrage territorial et la mesurabilité des actions sont des aspects très importants dont il faudra tenir compte au cours de l'élaboration du CPP. Le nouveau CPP devrait être disponible d'ici la fin du mois d'octobre 2026. Armelle Ouédraogo Lefaso.net

items.title: Heart of the Beast to Practical Magic 2: 10 of the best films to watch this September
items.description: From a Brad Pitt survival adventure with a canine co-star, to witchy sequel Practical Magic 2, starring Nicole Kidman and Sandra Bullock, here are the films to watch at the cinema this month. (Credit: Sony Pictures) 1. Resident Evil Zach Cregger’s Weapons was one of 2025’s most acclaimed films, so in some ways it’s a surprise that he’s followed it up with a video game spin-off. But the writer-director told Empire that he has made “a Zach Cregger movie that just happens to be a Resident Evil movie”. Far spookier-looking than the previous Resident Evil films, most of which were directed by Paul WS Anderson, this blood-drenched reboot focuses on a medical courier, Bryan (Austin Abrams). He has the job of delivering an organ to a hospital in the game’s main location, Raccoon City – but the city’s inhabitants are turning into ravenous zombies. “Bryan is very much an everyman who happens to be burdened with this sacred mission that’s going to take him into the heart of everything,” says Cregger. “It’s kind of like Frodo [from The Lord of the Rings] going into Mordor.” Released internationally on 16, 17 and 18 September (Credit: A24) 2. Primetime The year of Robert Pattinson continues. As well as appearing in The Odyssey, The Drama and the forthcoming Dune: Part Three, the British actor is starring in Primetime, a fact-based drama about a controversial reality television show, To Catch a Predator. From 2004 to 2007, each episode of the programme revolved around sting operations in which men were tricked into thinking that they were meeting children for sexual encounters. They would then be confronted by the journalist behind the sting, Chris Hansen. Pattinson plays Hansen, and he is already being tipped as an Oscar contender – even if Hansen himself would have chosen a different actor for the role. “Years ago I had crafted a screenplay and thought Denis Leary would be a good guy to play me,” he said on the Serialously podcast . Released on 25 September in the US and Canada (Credit: Courtesy of Sundance Festival) 3. The Weight Ethan Hawke follows his Oscar-nominated turn in Blue Moon with a very different kind of period drama. Set in Oregon during the Great Depression, The Weight stars Hawke as a single father who is unfairly sent to a labour camp. If he doesn’t get home soon, he will lose custody of his young daughter, but the devilish warden (Russell Crowe) promises to free him on one condition: he and a team of other prisoners have to carry knapsacks full of stolen gold bricks across the country. “Hawke is mesmerising,” says Chase Hutchinson in The Wrap . “The action scenes are tense and well-executed, though it’s the way he grounds it that makes you feel every setback. Hawke makes you buy into every beat, whether haunting or thrilling as the film grows more violent… You can’t look away for even a second.” Released on 18 September in the US and Canada (Credit: Warner Bros Pictures) 4. Practical Magic 2 Back in 1998, Nicole Kidman and Sandra Bullock starred in Practical Magic as Gillian and Sally, two sisters who were also witches. When the film came out, audiences weren’t exactly spellbound, but the dark supernatural romance gradually built a cult following. “I don’t know any woman who’s watched the movie and not wanted Gillian’s red hair, Sally’s cosy yet witchy outfits, or the beautiful Victorian house by the ocean that the family lives in,” wrote Tove Danovich in Country Living recently. Now, 28 years after the first film, a sequel is finally here. Once again, it’s adapted from a novel by Alice Hoffman, and once again Kidman and Bullock have the lead roles. Stockard Channing and Dianne Wiest are back as their aunts, and Joey King and Maisie Williams join the cast as Sally’s daughters, two young women who learn about the family curse: any man they fall in love with will die soon afterwards. Released on 11 September in the US, the UK and Ireland, and on 18 September in Canada and Australia (Credit: Universal Pictures) 5. Forgotten Island The latest cartoon from DreamWorks Animation (The Wild Robot, Dog Man) is a psychedelic fantasy adventure – but it’s also the first major Hollywood film to draw on Filipino folklore. Grammy-winning singer H.E.R. and Liza Soberano provide the voices of Jo and Raissa, two schoolgirls who become best friends in the Philippines in the 1990s. Years later, Raissa is about to emigrate to the US, but before she can go, the two girls fall through a portal into a magical world of demons, witches and monsters. And if they stay there too long, their memories of each other will fade away. “So many times, young girls in movies and TV are portrayed as always talking about boys, or they’re princesses,” the film’s co-director, Joel Crawford, said in Variety . “I want my [Filipina] daughters to see themselves up on the screen, whether it’s in terms of culture, in terms of ethnicity, but also how they are as people.” Released on 25 September in the US and Canada and 16 October in the UK and Ireland (Credit: A24) 6. Onslaught Michael Biehn co-starred in The Terminator and Aliens, two classic science-fiction thrillers in which a rugged heroine fought an almost indestructible foe. And now he’s appearing in a film which he says deserves to be compared to them. Released by A24, and directed by Adam Wingard (The Guest, Godzilla vs Kong), Onslaught stars Adria Arjona as a single mother who lives in a desert trailer park with her daughter. When three genetically modified super soldiers escape from a local secret research facility, her experience as an army sniper comes in handy. “I’m telling you without a doubt, this is the best movie I’ve been in since Aliens,” said Biehn in Daily Dead . “This is going to blow the doors off of any expectations of what anybody has seen on the big screen in a long time. This is like pedal-to-the-metal action, horror, violence… It is very, very exciting, and it’s fast and furious.” Released on 4 September in the US and Canada (Credit: Paramount Pictures) 7. Heart of the Beast Good news for fans of wilderness survival adventures: there are two of them in cinemas this September. As well as The Weight, there is Heart of the Beast, starring Brad Pitt and directed by David Ayer. Pitt plays a wounded Special Forces veteran who has to trek back to civilisation after a plane crash in a remote Alaskan forest. Luckily for him, he is accompanied by his faithful military dog, Odin. Ayer said in GQ that Pitt is on career-best form: “A constant theme from people who have seen the film is just how raw and believable and profound his performance is.” But Uber, the mountain-rescue dog who plays Odin, may be even better. “The one spoiler I’ll forward right now is, don’t worry, the dog lives,” reveals Ayer. Regardless, he says “I’ve shown the film to a few of my roughneck, tough-guy friends, and they’re crying at the end of this. I’ve never had a film move an audience so powerfully.” Released internationally on 24 and 25 September (Credit: Getty Images) 8. Knife: The Attempted Murder of Salman Rushdie On 12 August 2022, the author Sir Salman Rushdie was giving a talk in New York state, when someone in the audience leapt on stage and stabbed him 15 times . But Sir Salman wouldn’t be silenced. He wrote a memoir about the horrific attack and his recovery, and now the book has been turned into a documentary by Alex Gibney (Taxi to the Dark Side). Using intimate footage shot by Sir Salman’s wife, Rachel Eliza Griffiths, Gibney looks back at the ordeal, explores the author’s life and philosophy, and recalls how the publication of his 1988 novel, Satanic Verses, led to Iran’s Ayatollah Khomeini calling on him to be killed. “Throughout the film, three things stand out,” says Amber Wilkinson in Screen International , “the love between Rushdie and Griffiths; the resilience they had in the face of his catastrophic injuries; and the author’s humanistic attitude and sly sense of humour, which have categorically survived intact.” Released on 17 September in the US and 30 September in the UK (Credit: Focus Features) 9. The Uprising Step aside, Robin Hood. The Uprising is a medieval epic about English rebels fighting back against the greedy aristocracy, but rather than rehashing old myths and legends, Paul Greengrass (Captain Phillips, The Bourne Supremacy) has dramatised the English Peasant’s Revolt of 1381. Andrew Garfield plays the Robin Hood-alike hero, a poverty-stricken farmer known only as Ploughman. After his family is wiped out by the plague, he leads a resistance movement against the soldiers of the teenage King Richard II (Woody Norman). “It was sort of the first moment in our history when the common man and woman took centre stage,” said Greengrass in People , “and history was no longer going to be about kings and queens and the rich and powerful. It was going to be about what ordinary folk wanted and their grievances and their dreams and hopes.” Released on 11 September in the US and Canada (Credit: NEON) 10. Hope Hope is this year’s must-see monster movie – although it’s also a gritty western, a grisly horror film, a gonzo action comedy, and a cosmic science-fiction saga. Written and directed by Na Hong-jin, it features Hwang Jung-min as the tough sheriff of a small Korean coastal town. Within minutes of the opening scene, he is on the trail of a giant ogre which is laying waste to everything in its path. And the chaos doesn’t let up for another two and a half hours. Hope is “a full-on, unapologetic action movie packed with breathtaking and breathless car chases, horse chases, foot-chases and monster chases”, says John Bleasdale in Sight and Sound . “Brilliantly crafted and beautifully shot, we can only hope this wild film gets the follow-up it so richly deserves.” Released on 9 September in the US, 10 September in Australia and 25 September in the UK

items.title: Ioba/IPO : Le haut-commissaire et les journalistes passent une journée sur le site des appelés
items.description: Burkina/Ioba-Immersion-Patriotique-Obligatoire Ioba/IPO : Le haut-commissaire et les journalistes passent une journée sur le site des appelés Dano, 20 août 2026 (AIB) – À l’occasion de la Journée des médias, le haut-commissaire de la province du Ioba, Innocents Ouattara, a assisté à la montée des couleurs nationales, suivie de l’exécution de l’ordre serré, sur le site des appelées filles du centre de Dano, le jeudi 13 août 2026, en présence des hommes de médias. La montée des couleurs nationales sur le site de l’Immersion patriotique obligatoire (IPO) a connu la présence du premier responsable du Ioba, Innocents Ouattara. Il était accompagné des membres de la cellule provinciale d’organisation de l’IPO et des hommes de médias. Une appelée a été invitée au mât pour la montée du pavillon national. Les autres ont entonné en chœur l’hymne de la victoire, le Ditanyè. Elles ont ainsi exprimé leur attachement aux valeurs patriotiques. À l’issue de ce cérémonial, les appelées ont entamé l’exécution de l’ordre serré dans une discipline exemplaire. Elles ont émerveillé les visiteurs du jour par les exercices de marches cadencées, de demi-tours à gauche ou à droite, entre autres. Répondant aux questions des journalistes, l’appelée Djamila Soré a estimé que l’apprentissage de l’ordre serré est une bonne initiative. « On nous apprend à marcher dans la discipline », a-t-elle affirmé. Pour la déléguée des filles, Bertine Dabiré, « l’ordre serré est important parce qu’il permet de maintenir son corps tout en tenant compte de notre environnement immédiat ». Selon l’appelée Tierta Eve Somé, cet exercice agit efficacement sur le corps humain. « L’ordre serré m’a permis de discipliner mon corps et mon esprit en tenant compte de ceux qui sont à côté de moi. Il a également créé une sociabilité avec les autres. C’est pourquoi, nous marchons ensemble comme une pyramide établie », a-t-elle confié. Une pause a été observée après cet exercice avant d’aller en salle pour suivre le module portant sur la souveraineté. Selon l’animateur Ibrahim Ouédraogo, ce module porte sur la souveraineté économique, sécuritaire, alimentaire, politique et culturelle. À l’issue du cours, l’appelée de l’IPO Laonta Elodie Somda a rappelé que la souveraineté sécuritaire d’un pays est la capacité de ce pays à prendre en charge la sécurité de sa population et de ses biens sans l’aide extérieure. Selon elle, la garantie de la sécurité concerne chaque citoyen. C’est pourquoi, elle a pris un engagement. « Je m’engage à informer les FDS si je découvre une situation douteuse et je vais sensibiliser mes proches sur la solidarité afin de renforcer la cohésion sociale ». Sur le plan économique, l’appelée Rasmata Ouédraogo trouve que le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré a mis le Burkina Faso sur la voie de la souveraineté économique. « Il a lancé les initiatives présidentielles pour inciter certains jeunes à l’entrepreneuriat et former d’autres à l’agriculture et l’élevage, socle de l’économie de notre pays », a-t-elle confié. Après ce cours, les journalistes ont rejoint les appelés garçons sur le site du Lycée provincial du Ioba (LPI). Là, l’animateur a organisé une séance de révision sur la géopolitique. Les appelés ont été invités à rappeler les différents points de ce module à leurs camarades, en s’exerçant à l’art oratoire. Plusieurs appelés ont réussi cet exercice avec succès, en français comme en Dagara. La fin de cette étape de la journée a été suivie par le repas. Le moral haut et très enthousiastes, les appelés ont chanté pendant que certains servaient le riz gras. Tout cela s’est passé en présence du premier responsable de la province, Innocents Ouattara. Les autorités et les hommes de médias ont pris congé des appelés après les encouragements du haut-commissaire à la bonne conduite pour les jours restants. Agence d’information du Burkina SZ-DNK

items.title: Ceuta entierra a los primeros migrantes fallecidos en la avalancha en El Tarajal
items.description: Tumbados sobre el lado derecho, con el rostro orientado hacia La Meca y con cuidado de que la tierra no toque sus cuerpos. Los primeros 18 fallecidos por la llegada masiva de migrantes a través del espigón fronterizo de Ceuta de los pasados 30 y 31 de julio, en la que murieron 82 personas , todos hombres salvo una mujer, han recibido sepultura final este viernes por la tarde en el cementerio musulmán de Sidi Embarek. El entierro, público, ha congregado a una docena de imanes de las mezquitas de la ciudad autónoma. Sus lápidas, identificadas con números porque no se conocen sus nombres ni sus historias, están conectadas con una causa judicial con los pocos datos que tiene de ellos: dónde les encontraron, características físicas, ropa y alguna peculiaridad que pueda relacionarles con los suyos. Solo nueve de los fallecidos han sido identificados y, de momento, Marruecos no acepta la entrega a sus familias, ha explicado la consejera de Sanidad, Nabila Benzina. “No se conocen los motivos. La funeraria lo ha intentado dos veces. Alguna familia ha venido y ha podido velar a su ser querido, pero no reunirse con él en su país”, ha contado antes de que se comenzara el enterramiento. Benzina asegura que lo seguirán intentando, aunque tampoco tienen mucho tiempo porque hay que cumplir las recomendaciones sanitarias. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Kidnappers flee as police rescue 75 victims in Birnin Gwari
items.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo Kaduna— The Kaduna State Police Command has rescued 75 kidnapped victims, including men, women and children, who were abducted by armed men in Folwaya Village, near Birnin Gwari. The victims, identified as Fulani travellers, were reportedly abducted while travelling in commercial buses on Wednesday. The Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Mansir Hassan, who disclosed this in a statement ,said the incident occurred at about 5:30pm on August 19, 2026, following information received from the National Union of Road Transport Workers, NURTW, Birnin Gwari branch. According to him, the victims were abducted by unknown gunmen armed with AK-47 rifles and other sophisticated weapons and taken into a forest. He said the abductors subsequently concealed the victims in a cave located within a mountainous area. Hassan said that upon receiving the information, a crack team from the Birnin Gwari Area Command was immediately deployed to the location. He added that the operatives’ arrival forced the kidnappers to flee, abandoning the victims, who were rescued unharmed. The Commissioner of Police, Kaduna State Command, CP Rabiu Muhammad, commended the NURTW, Birnin Gwari branch, for providing the police with timely and vital information that facilitated the rescue operation. He also praised the Area Commander, Birnin Gwari, and his operatives for their swift and professional response. The CP urged residents to remain vigilant and promptly report suspicious movements and activities to the police. He, however, cautioned members of the public against taking the law into their own hands, warning that such actions could result in the loss of innocent lives. items.title: Gamou 2026 : le Président Bassirou Diomaye Faye salue l’œuvre d’éducation de Serigne Moustapha Sy
items.description: Le président de la République, Bassirou Diomaye Diakhar Faye, a achevé, vendredi, sa visite à Tivaouane par une audience avec Serigne Moustapha Sy, responsable moral du Dahiratoul Moustarchidina Wal Moustarchidaty. À quelques jours du Gamou, le chef de l’État a transmis au guide religieux les salutations de la Nation, salué l’action spirituelle et citoyenne menée par le mouvement auprès de la jeunesse et sollicité des prières pour la paix ainsi que pour la réussite de sa mission à la tête du Sénégal. À quelques jours de la célébration du Mawlid, le président de la République a effectué une visite auprès de Serigne Moustapha Sy. Une audience qui intervient dans le cadre de la traditionnelle ziarra présidentielle à Tivaouane, à l’approche du Gamou. Au cours de cette rencontre, Bassirou Diomaye Faye a transmis à Serigne Moustapha Sy les salutations et le respect de l’ensemble de la Nation. Le chef de l’État a également tenu à mettre en lumière le rôle joué par le Dahiratoul Moustarchidina Wal Moustarchidaty dans l’éducation et l’encadrement de la jeunesse. Il a ainsi salué l’œuvre d’éducation spirituelle et citoyenne menée par le mouvement, qu’il inscrit dans la continuité de l’héritage de Seydi El Hadj Malick Sy. Un hommage qui donne une dimension particulière à cette audience, au moment où Tivaouane s’apprête à accueillir des milliers de fidèles pour la célébration du Gamou. Face au guide des Moustarchidines, le président de la République a également sollicité des prières pour la paix au Sénégal et la stabilité du pays. Bassirou Diomaye Faye a aussi demandé à Serigne Moustapha Sy de prier pour lui afin qu’il puisse réussir dans l’accomplissement de ses activités et de la mission que les Sénégalais lui ont confiée à la tête de l’État. Cette sollicitation de prières illustre la dimension spirituelle de la rencontre entre le chef de l’État et le responsable moral du Dahiratoul Moustarchidina Wal Moustarchidaty, à quelques jours de l’un des plus grands rendez-vous religieux du pays. À travers l’hommage rendu au mouvement, le président de la République a mis l’accent sur l’importance de l’éducation des jeunes et de la transmission des valeurs. L’action des Moustarchidines, tournée vers l’enseignement religieux, l’encadrement et la formation spirituelle et citoyenne, a ainsi été au cœur du message présidentiel. Cette reconnaissance intervient dans un contexte où la question de la jeunesse demeure au cœur des préoccupations nationales. L’éducation spirituelle et citoyenne participe également, selon cette vision, à la construction d'une société fondée sur la responsabilité, la solidarité et le respect des valeurs. L’audience avec Serigne Moustapha Sy a constitué la dernière étape de la visite du président de la République à Tivaouane. Plus tôt dans la journée, Bassirou Diomaye Faye avait été reçu par le Khalife général des Tidianes, Serigne Babacar Sy Mansour. En clôturant sa visite auprès de Serigne Moustapha Sy, le chef de l’État a ainsi placé cette étape sous le signe de la reconnaissance, de la spiritualité et de la confiance dans les prières des guides religieux. À la veille du Gamou, cette rencontre aura surtout été l’occasion pour Bassirou Diomaye Faye de rendre hommage au rôle éducatif des Moustarchidines, tout en sollicitant les prières de leur guide pour la paix au Sénégal et la réussite de sa mission présidentielle. Cheikh Tidiane NDIAYE
